body.statement:
For every coherent foldwise fit using \(\widehat R=\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B\widehat W\), the corrected \(\widehat N\), and the data-driven spectral inverse, if \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1)\), then, on an event whose probability tends to one, \(\|E_P(\widehat U-\widehat Q\widehat U)-\psi\|\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\Delta_n\), where
\[
 \Delta_n=r_m(r_\pi+r_A+r_Z)+r_Ar_Z+(r_A+r_Z)R_\Sigma
 +\ell_{A,n}+\ell_{Z,n}.
\]
In particular, the pathwise derivative of the mean bias is zero along a support-preserving two-sided perturbation of \(M_A\) alone and along a coherent perturbation of \(f\) alone.
body.justification: The cancellation shows that the finite efficiency correction preserves orthogonality when all fitted objects arise from one product law.
body.gap: Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen establish mixed bias for their binary score, while the new projected \(K\)-class correction introduces posterior and Gram errors not covered by that expansion.
body.consumer: It permits flexible learning of exposure misclassification and birth-weight regressions under explicit product-rate conditions.
body.proof_tex:
Work coordinatewise and put \(k=QU\) and \(\widehat k=\widehat Q\widehat U\).  The support-leakage conditional-zero lemma applies to the same coherent fitted law and the same data-driven spectral inverse.  On its event \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{supp},n}\), whose probability tends to one when \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1)\), it gives
\[
 \|E_P\widehat k\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\left[
 (r_A+r_Z)\|\widehat k-k\|_{L^2(P)}+r_Ar_Z
 +\ell_{A,n}+\ell_{Z,n}\right]. \tag{50}
\]
Lemma 6 implies \(\|\widehat k-k\|_2\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma\), so
\[
 \|E_P\widehat k\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\{(r_A+r_Z)R_\Sigma+r_Ar_Z
 +\ell_{A,n}+\ell_{Z,n}\}. \tag{51}
\]

It remains to control the raw bridge mean.  Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \delta^A_{j\ell}(X)
 &=E_P\{\widehat a_j(A,X)\mid J=\ell,X\}-\mathbf 1\{j=\ell\},\\
 \delta^Z_{j\ell}(X)
 &=E_P\{\widehat z_j(Z,X)\mid J=\ell,X\}-\mathbf 1\{j=\ell\}. \tag{52}
\end{aligned}
\]
Conditional three-view independence and direct expansion of \(\widehat U_j\) give the exact identity
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_P(\widehat U_j\mid X)-m_j
={}&(\widehat m_j-m_j)
 \left[1-\frac{\pi_j}{\widehat\pi_j}
 (1+\delta^A_{jj})(1+\delta^Z_{jj})\right]\\
&+\widehat\pi_j^{-1}\sum_{\ell\ne j}\pi_\ell
 \delta^A_{j\ell}\delta^Z_{j\ell}(m_\ell-\widehat m_j). \tag{53}
\end{aligned}
\]
For example, the term indexed by \(\ell\) uses
\(E_P(Y-\widehat m_j\mid J=\ell,X)=m_\ell-\widehat m_j\), while the two bridges factor conditionally.  The inverse identity (46) gives
\[
 \|\delta^A\|_2\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_A,
 \qquad \|\delta^Z\|_2\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_Z. \tag{54}
\]
Using the true and fitted propensity lower bounds, \(|m_j|\vee|\widehat m_j|\leq L\), Cauchy--Schwarz, and (53)--(54), then integrating over \(X\), yields
\[
 \|E_P\widehat U-\psi\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\{r_m(r_\pi+r_A+r_Z)+r_Ar_Z\}. \tag{55}
\]
Since the estimated efficient score is \(\widehat U-\widehat k\), the triangle inequality applied to (51) and (55) proves the stated \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}\Delta_n\) bound, including both first-order leakage allowances.

For a support-preserving two-sided path perturbing only \(M_A\), the leakage terms are zero, (55) is exactly zero because \(\widehat m=m\), \(\widehat\pi=\pi\), and \(\delta^Z=0\), while (50) is \(O(r_A^2)\) by Lemma 6.  Its mean-bias derivative is therefore zero.  If only \(f\) is perturbed coherently, then \(\widehat B=B\), so \(B^{\mathsf T}\widehat k=0\) makes \(E_P\widehat k=0\) exactly; also \(\delta^A=\delta^Z=0\), and (53) is zero exactly.  This proves the two stated first-order cancellations without suppressing unrestricted-support leakage.
